papers.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

papers.title: On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group
papers.abstract: The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.

papers.title: Nonsolvable critical groups with the spectrum of $S_{10}$
papers.abstract: We classify the nonsolvable finite groups that are critical with respect to the spectrum of the symmetric group $S_{10}$. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: $S_{10}$ and $(A_9\times C_3)\rtimes C_2$, where the involution acts on $A_9$ by conjugation by a transposition and on $C_3$ by inversion. The quotient of any nonsolvable group with this spectrum by its solvable radical is almost simple. All possible simple socles are treated without assuming that the radical is nilpotent. The final cases, $L_3(4)$ and $A_6$, are excluded using the canonical subgroup $K=[R(G)\cap G^\infty,G^\infty]$, actions on chief factors, and the required element orders $9,20,30$. In the $A_6$ case, the final contradiction is the existence of an element of order $16$. Reproducible certificates accompany the character-table and matrix calculations.

papers.title: Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity
papers.abstract: For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $\alpha$ satisfying the condition \[ \{g^{a_0}\cdot\alpha(g)^{a_1}\cdots\alpha^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $\iota(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.

papers.title: The distortion of finitely generated subgroups in hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We show that the range of distortion functions of finitely generated subgroups of hyperbolic groups is essentially as broad as the range of time-complexity functions $T(n)$ of Turing machines. More precisely, we show that for each such $T(n) \geq n$ for which $T(n)^3$ is superadditive, there is a hyperbolic group $G$ with a finitely generated normal subgroup $N$ such that $\text{Dist}_N^G(n) \simeq 2^{T(n)^3}$. Our approach is to estimate the distortion of the kernels in Wise's HNN version of the Rips construction, and then to look at what these estimates yield when the $S$-machine groups of Sapir, Birget, and Rips are the inputs to the construction.
